key_insight: The paper shows that the usual gap between homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous optimization is not easily closed: common similarity and weak interpolation assumptions are provably too weak, and only a stronger combination of interpolation and local PL conditions yields a better time bound.
engineering_relevance: For distributed ML systems, this clarifies which assumptions are actually needed to justify faster asynchronous training with non-identical worker data, helping guide algorithm design and expected speedups.
method: Proves impossibility results under widely used first- and second-order similarity assumptions for randomized algorithms.
Tests the weak interpolation regime and shows it still cannot recover the homogeneous-style complexity.
Derives a new time complexity bound using strong interpolation plus a local Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and complexity bounds rather than experiments, with the main evaluation being proof-based comparison of assumptions and asymptotic time complexity.
watch_item: The improved bound depends on strong, problem-specific assumptions, so it may not apply to many real heterogeneous training workloads.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
